title: Extra-Scriptural teaching is rejectable as human — Scripture the examination rule
source_text: XXVIII. Denique quod tradunt & docent Ecclesiae Doctores non potest rejici tanquam humana traditio, nisi quia est extra Scripturam. Etenim, si Dei verbum Scriptura sacra determinatum non esset, sed praeterea extaret verbum Dei non scriptum, jure possent obtendere Ecclesiae Doctores sua documenta esse illud ipsum Dei verbum. Et revera, si ad aliquod verbum Dei non scriptum nobis recurrendum esset, unde potius deberet accipi quam ab ipsis? Cum ergo nihilominus contingat, teste Christo, Ecclesiae Doctores pro Dei verbo proponere quod non est aliud quam humanum commentum; inde manifestum est habendum esse pro doctrina hominum, quicquid extra Scripturae substantiam proponi potest, & Scripturam regulam esse ad quam omnia examinanda sunt: alioquin, ut diximus, Magistrorum Ecclesiae praecepta & documenta, tanquam traditiones humanae, rejici non possent.
pass_a_gloss: Finally, what the Church's doctors hand down and teach cannot be rejected as a human tradition except because it is outside Scripture. For if the word of God were not bounded by sacred Scripture, but besides that an unwritten word of God also existed, the Church's doctors could justly claim that their documents are that very word of God. And indeed, if we had to have recourse to some unwritten word of God, from whom should it rather be received than from them? Since therefore it nevertheless happens, Christ being witness, that the Church's doctors propose as God's word what is nothing other than a human invention — from this it is plain that whatever can be proposed outside the substance of Scripture must be held as the doctrine of men, and that Scripture is the rule by which all things are to be examined: otherwise, as we have said, the precepts and documents of the Church's teachers could not be rejected as human traditions.
pass_b_english: Church teachers' delivery can be rejected as human tradition only because it stands outside Scripture.

If God's word were not bounded by Scripture and an unwritten divine word also existed, teachers could rightly claim their teaching is that word — and if we needed an unwritten word, where else would we take it?
Yet Christ shows Church doctors can propose mere human invention as God's word.

Therefore whatever can be proposed outside Scripture's substance counts as human doctrine, and Scripture is the rule for examining all things — otherwise magisterial precepts could never be rejected as human traditions.

lemmas.gloss: except because it is outside Scripture

choices.why: Word of God delimited to Scripture.
